newsitem.title: EGYPT: Nine bodies found from capsized Egypt tourist boat.
newsitem.headline: Nine bodies found from capsized Egypt tourist boat.

text.p: Nine bodies have been recovered from the wreck of a Nile cruiser which capsized on Thursday, diplomats said, and Egyptian rescuers were searching on Monday for up to 11 people still missing.

More than 100 people aboard the Amira Jihan survived after the cruiser, carrying 77 mostly Czech and Slovak tourists and 51 Egyptian crew and tour guides, capsized in a freak storm in southern Egypt four days ago.
The Interior Ministry said on Monday rescuers were searching for 11 people still missing -- five tourists and six Egyptians.

"The divers are still looking for the two Czechs and three Slovaks. We think they are in the cabins that are underwater but the problem is that there is so much furniture and debris that it's difficult to get to them," Vratisalv Janda, consul at the Czech embassy in Cairo, told Reuters.
Rescue teams were trying to right the boat which is lying half-submerged on its left side, he said.
Janda said divers found the bodies of a Czech and a Slovak on Sunday afternoon. They were not identified.
The bodies of four Czechs, two Slovaks and a Pole had been retrieved on Friday and Saturday.
Janda said most of the tourists who survived the accident had left for home on Sunday and Monday.
Cairo newspapers said the bodies of three of the Egyptians listed as missing by the Interior Ministry had been found. There was no official confirmation of the report.
The cruiser, which tipped over in the Nile about 580 km (360 miles) south of Cairo, was making the popular trip from Aswan to Luxor, passing by the Pharaonic temples of Kom Ombo, Edfu and Esna.
It was the worst accident on a Nile cruiser for many years, though disasters with local ferries in Egypt are more common.
